recognize_zh: 拼圖中的淋巴球、嗜中性球與單核球樣細胞，細胞質內都有數顆比一般顆粒大很多、粉紫到灰紫色、形狀不規則的巨大顆粒（giant granules）；多種白血球同時出現巨大包涵顆粒，就是 Chediak-Higashi 症候群的典型表現。
features: Composite of peripheral blood leukocytes with abnormally large cytoplasmic granules
Lymphocytes containing one to several large azurophilic inclusions
Neutrophils and band forms with coarse, enlarged pink-violet to gray granules
Mononuclear cells with multiple large irregular purple granules around the nucleus
Granules markedly larger than normal primary or secondary granules; nuclei otherwise unremarkable
describe_en: Composite of peripheral blood leukocytes shows abnormally large, irregular pink-violet to gray cytoplasmic granules in multiple lineages, including lymphocytes with one to several giant azurophilic inclusions, segmented and band neutrophils with coarse enlarged granules, and mononuclear cells with large perinuclear granules. The granules are considerably larger than normal neutrophil granules, and nuclear morphology is otherwise unremarkable. Findings are consistent with Chediak-Higashi syndrome, due to LYST mutation; correlation with partial oculocutaneous albinism, hair shaft examination, and genetic testing is recommended.

ddx.vs: Toxic granules are numerous small dark azurophilic granules evenly distributed in neutrophils only, rather than few giant granules across lineages.
Alder-Reilly granules are dense, uniform, dark purple granules filling the cytoplasm of all leukocytes, not sparse giant irregular inclusions.
Pseudo-Chediak-Higashi granules occur in dysplastic or leukemic myeloid cells with blasts or dysplasia and without albinism.
Normal LGLs contain several small azurophilic granules in abundant cytoplasm, not giant inclusions.
